title: Palashi / Plassey
subtitle: Site of the 1757 Battle That Changed Bengal's History
description: A small village in Bengal where the 1757 Battle of Plassey took place, marking the beginning of British colonial rule in India. The battlefield witnessed the defeat of Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah by the East India Company's forces under Robert Clive.

seoTitle: Palashi (Plassey): 1757 Battlefield and Bengal's Colonial Turning Point
seoDescription: Explore the site of the 1757 Battle of Plassey (Palashi), where British forces defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah, marking the beginning of colonial rule in Bengal and India.

faq.question: Why is it called both Palashi and Plassey?
faq.answer: Palashi is the Bengali name, derived from the Palash tree (Butea monosperma or Flame of the Forest) that grew in the area. Plassey is the English romanization used in British colonial records.

faq.question: What happened at the Battle of Plassey?
faq.answer: On June 23, 1757, the forces of the East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj ud-Daulah's army. The battle was decided by betrayal—key commanders like Mir Jafar defected to the British side. This victory gave the British control over Bengal and marked the beginning of colonial rule in India.

faq.question: Where exactly is Palashi located?
faq.answer: Palashi is a small village in Nadia District of West Bengal, India, located on the east bank of the Bhagirathi River, about 50 km north of Krishnanagar and approximately 150 km from Kolkata.
